question: A 24-year-old woman requests a copper IUCD for contraception. She is currently being treated for pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) diagnosed 5 days ago. According to WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC), insertion of a copper IUCD now would be classified as:

answers.text: WHO MEC Category 1 — no restriction; IUCD can be inserted to provide contraception during PID treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MEC Category 1 means a condition for which there are no restrictions. Active PID is not in this category — insertion into an infected uterus risks ascending infection, failure of PID treatment, and increased risk of tubo-ovarian abscess.

answers.text: WHO MEC Category 2 — the advantages generally outweigh the risks; proceed with counselling

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MEC Category 2 indicates advantages outweigh risks. Active PID does not fall here — it is an absolute contraindication because inserting a foreign body into an actively infected uterus worsens the infection.

answers.text: WHO MEC Category 4 — absolute contraindication; IUCD must NOT be inserted

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Active PID (current or within the last 3 months) is a WHO MEC Category 4 absolute contraindication for IUCD insertion. The device must not be inserted until the infection has been fully treated and resolved.

answers.text: WHO MEC Category 3 — the risks generally outweigh the advantages; avoid if possible but can be used if necessary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MEC Category 3 means the risks generally outweigh the advantages. Active PID is stricter — it is Category 4 (absolute contraindication), not Category 3.

overallFeedback.feedback: Active PID is a WHO MEC Category 4 absolute contraindication for IUCD insertion. Inserting an IUCD into an infected uterus risks spreading infection, causing tubo-ovarian abscess, and failure of antibiotic treatment.
Correct. Active PID is WHO MEC Category 4 for IUCD insertion. The device must not be inserted until the infection has been fully treated.
